newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan gains China backing on Hong Kong consulate.
newsitem.headline: Japan gains China backing on Hong Kong consulate.

text.p: Japan and China signed on Saturday an agreement allowing Tokyo to maintain its consulate in Hong Kong after the territory reverts to Beijing rule later this year.

Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda signed the accord with his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen during his official visit to Beijing, Japanese Foreign Ministry spokesman Hidehiko Hamada told reporters.

China is to resume sovereignty over the British colony of Hong Kong on July 1 this year and a number of countries with consulates in the territory have been waiting for final word from Beijing on whether the offices can remain in place after the handover.
The United States won backing from Beijing earlier this week to keep its consulate during a visit to China by U.S. Vice-President Al Gore.
